rulings.restated: Enter the amount from qbi helper "Taxable income before the QBI deduction; Form 1040 line 11a minus lines 12e and 13b, floored at zero".
rulings.model: The instructions say 'Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a, minus lines 12e and 13b' with no floor, but the program floors the result at zero. That changes the line 11 value when the result is negative, although line 13 makes the final deduction the same.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The helper floors line 11 at zero where the corrected instruction ('Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a, minus lines 12e and 13b', i8995-correction) states no floor. A negative and a zero line 11 give the same line 12 comparison and the same line 13 ('if zero or less, enter -0-'), so the deduction is unchanged; a printed line 11 would read 0 where the form would show a negative amount. No change to the data.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from qbi helper "Add sd.net_gain, f1040.line3a".
rulings.model: The program always takes net capital gain from Schedule D lines 15/16. The instructions add: 'If you're not required to file Schedule D (Form 1040), your net capital gain is the amount reported on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a.' That case is omitted and no refusal covers it.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. For a Schedule D filer the helper is the smaller of Schedule D lines 15 and 16, floored at zero, plus Form 1040 line 3a, as the instructions say. When Schedule D is not required (i8995 p. 4: "your net capital gain is the amount reported on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a") the Schedule D lines are still computed from line 13 alone, so lines 15 and 16 both equal the box 2a total that line 7a carries, and the helper gives the same amount. No change to the data.
